summary: ```markdown # CLO 2025.2 - Piece Editor In this video, I will introduce you to the main function of the 2025.2 version, the paper editor, to help you improve the product design to a new level. Now you can directly define the structure of the paper in the 3D project, implement editing, and accurately simulate the shrinkage effect. The design experience is fully upgraded. ## Workflow Overview Let's take a closer look at the workflow: 1. **Select Fabric**: First, select a fabric in the object window. 2. **Change Material Type**: In the property editor, change the material type to a wool product. ## New Features In the 2025.2 version, you can see a new needle ball icon. Open the paper editor by clicking to open it. The window of the paper editor will appear in the 2D window. You can click on the option card at the bottom to switch. ### Draft Adjustment It is very easy to guide the draft. You can use a space similar to the window in the 3D window to adjust the draft in the editor. - **Navigate Draft**: - Press the middle key and move the mouse wheel to parallel the draft. - Rotate the middle key wheel to enlarge and shrink the draft. - Press the right mouse key and move the mouse to rotate the draft around the center freely. - Hold the mouse wheel to make time-catches. - Use the mouse wheel to expand the left and right sizes. Pinch it further to load the whole screen. ### System Modes and Views - **Switch Modes**: Press the switch to change to any system mode. - **Preset Views**: Press the shortcut button to switch to the desired preset view at any time. ### Sand Line Display You can use three types of sand line display to check the paper: - **Thick Sand Line**: Shows the actual thickness in pure color. - **Thin Sand Line**: Automatically displays the structure of the needle to enhance visibility. - **Random Color**: The color of the thread is used randomly, with each line using a different color to easily check the thread structure. ## Core Settings Next is the core setting. Here you can set the size of the piece of paper and the final output size. - **Set Specific Data**: - Enter the number of the sample cycle in the direction of the thread density. - Enter the number of hours by the signal type as you see on the screen in Starburg. ### Line Thickness and Density You can set the line thickness in millimeters and adjust the density of the line circle. Click on the icon to see more evidence options. The link shows the automatic measurement value of the current result, or you can click to cancel the link. - **Final Piece Size**: Enter the final piece size after shrink, such as the number of rows per inch and the thickness of the fabric. Change the line thickness and adjust the number of rows per inch. ### Real Sample Update After the thickness of the fabric is set, the real sample will be automatically updated. Please note that you do not need to click the reset piece button. If you want to understand the definition of the setting, you can hover over the setting to check the tooltips. ## Editing Process Start editing by selecting the needle type from the menu on the right or using the shortcut key. Support four options, including: - **Front Needle Bed**: Shortcut key is Q. - **Back Needle Bed**: Shortcut key is W. - **Front Loop Needle (Not Edited)**: Shortcut key is 1. - **Back Loop Needle (Not Edited)**: Shortcut key is 2. You can click and drag the piece to perform real needle editing. ## Simulation and Application After the sample design is completed, press the simulation button or press the control key. You can use your evidence and custom settings to apply the shrink effect. You will see that the piece structure presents a curve due to shrink. - **Continue Editing**: You can continue to edit during simulation activation and also update the shrink effect. - **Pause Simulation**: Press the simulation button or press the control key to pause. - **Apply Design**: To apply your piece design to the costume, press the application button to use the result in 3D costume, or press the application and close to apply the result and close the editor. If you just want to disregard the changes, press cancel. ## Result Checking In the 3D window, you can check the result and make further changes in the editor. After changes, press the application button or the application and close. The editor will add a new one. ### Thread Line Settings When the piece editor is opened, the thread line is thin. The number of rows per inch and the thickness of the fabric will be used to ensure that all changes are managed through the piece editor. After closing the piece editor, these options will be available again, allowing you to make further adjustments and check the 3D effect immediately. ## Final Adjustments Next, you can adjust the thread line settings in the property editor, such as the color of the thread line and the color of the bone thread. After completion, you can save this fabric for the next application, allowing for more flexible performance with the seamless division function. This step-by-step stitch change allows you to use the piece editor to create more accurate and complex digital piece designs. ```
